extracted.intended_audience: general public and scientific researchers interested in reproducibility and cancer research
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and procedural considerations for reproducing laboratory cancer experiments across different labs, including transparency, materials sharing, method detail, and resource/time requirements for replication efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility as a central feature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reproducibility is a central feature of how science is supposed to be" — experiments should yield consistent results when repeated by other researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use replication attempts to test core findings; treat successful replication as evidence supporting a result and failure to replicate as a signal to investigate causes rather than immediately discard the original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of study selection and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The reproducibility project "made sure this project was transparent about how it picked the studies, transparent about their methods and their study plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and publish criteria for choosing studies, full methods, and pre-specified study plans to allow others to evaluate and reproduce the replication effort; secrecy (e.g., not saying which experiments were examined) prevents follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability/sharing of original materials and reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Original labs providing critical materials helped replication attempts ("the lab gave us the same drug... they gave us the same tumor cells that they used").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing the exact reagents, cell lines, and materials used in the original experiment reduces ambiguity and removes a potential source of discrepancy between original and replication results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient methodological detail in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A possible reason for failed replication is that "the directions offered in a paper [are] too sketchy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original publications should include detailed protocols, conditions, and procedural steps so other labs can reproduce the experiment without needing implicit knowledge; vague methods are an anti-pattern that impedes replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique sensitivity and need for optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Some experiments may only work under particular conditions and "it can take months or years to perfect the laboratory techniques used in any given experiment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that successful replication can require iterative optimization and technical learning; brief replication windows may fail not because the original finding was false but because nuanced technique was not mastered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate time and resources for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Replication teams may be limited: "they have limited time and resources to spend on any one study... they can't go back and do these things over and over again when the first attempts turn out to be uninterpretable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design replication efforts with sufficient time, funding, and capacity for repeated attempts and troubleshooting; single, under-resourced attempts can yield uninterpretable or misleading results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify patterns and common causes of non-reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The project is "looking for patterns across cancer research and also trying to identify common reasons that labs might have trouble reproducing one another's work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyze multiple replication attempts to detect systematic issues (e.g., methodological gaps, reagent variability, context sensitivity) rather than treating each failed replication in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to cooperative follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Some original labs "cooperated" and even "went the extra mile to help the follow-up labs reduce potential sources of error."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage collaboration between original and replication teams (protocol walkthroughs, sharing tacit knowledge) to clarify ambiguous steps and reduce non-scientific sources of discrepancy; lack of cooperation can hinder meaningful interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing replication outcomes as investigations of 'why' rather than blame
rubrics_metrics.description: "The point isn't who's right and wrong but all about the why."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret replication successes and failures primarily as information about mechanisms, boundary conditions, and methodological robustness, not as a simple verdict on researchers' competence; use outcomes to improve practices and patient-relevant implications.
